headline: Mod installs, smoother controls and new inspection tools land
summary: Players can install mods from the signed index with dependencies, automatic updates and rollback, while diagonal stick movement now keeps pace with straight pushes. Windows fixes address sound gaps, missing Orxon barrier strands and blue explosion debris on Batalia; Pokitaru's underwater visibility is corrected on both renderers. Contributors gain an Object Viewer, freecam and better crash and lighting-bake logs, alongside phone GPU optimisations and more Android graphics controls.
highlights: The mod hub work in #161 had not yet run on Windows, macOS or Android. Add to Steam in #184 was tested on Linux; Windows and macOS still need manual checks, and Flatpak Steam is refused.
Mod SDK 1.11.0 adds a mod data folder and the current save slot, checked on PAL and NTSC (#172).
Object Viewer and Forward+ lighting land in #195, but experimental light editing, gizmos, bone attachments and JSON profiles remain behind a flag that defaults off.

Audio replacement #164 is open, while co-op #166 and Going Commando's native port #191 remain unmerged drafts. The latter builds and runs but is not playable; ship controls are incomplete and much of the menus is untested.
The day's 138,618 added and 49,327 deleted lines are dominated by the decompilation import #160: 111,618 additions and 47,520 deletions.
Vulkan tests reuse setup and change scheduling while retaining the full Enhanced suite (#163, #198). Lighting preparation issues #159 and #173 closed.
